quick.summary: Why finding the cause can wait, and the first three moves in a data incident.
quick.takeaway: Stop it spreading, tell people, then find the cause.

beats.line: Bad prices were loading into reports. I spent two hours finding why. Was that right?
For two hours, bad prices kept arriving. Order matters.
First, stop it spreading. Pause the job.
Second, tell the people using it. What is wrong, and until when.
If I pause it, reports go stale.
Stale and known beats fresh and wrong.
Job paused. Prices since nine are wrong. Next update at noon.
Now you can look for the cause without the clock running.

quiz.question: Wrong data is flowing into reports right now. What should you do first?
options: Pause the job so no more bad data arrives
quiz.explanation: Stopping the spread limits the damage; the cause can be found once it is contained.

quiz.question: During a data incident, slightly stale data is usually better than fresh wrong data.
quiz.explanation: People can work around data they know is old, but wrong data leads to wrong decisions.
